subject: FinApps: Persistent 5xx/429 + VPC/NAT timeouts — executive engagement requested
messages:
From: Rita Gomez <rita.gomez@finapps.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: 5xx/429 surge impacting checkout (FinApps)

Hi Marissa,

We're seeing a sharp increase in 5xx and 429 responses from the Redwood Dedicated endpoint over the last 45 minutes. Our checkout flows are timing out (~10s TTL) and retries are spiking which is compounding the load. Sample 429s attached.

What we know so far:
- Errors started ~07:30 PDT, coincident with a deployment on our side.
- Observed error types: 502, 504, 429.
- Latency for successful requests has jumped from ~120ms to ~1.2s.
- No changes to our VPC peering config.

Can you escalate to your ops/team? This is affecting revenue. We need an ETA for mitigation and any recommended short-term workarounds (rate-limiting, alternate region).

Thanks,
Rita
VP Ops, FinApps

Attachments: finapps_429_snippet.log (text/plain)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Rita Gomez <rita.gomez@finapps.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: 5xx/429 surge impacting checkout (FinApps)

Rita — thanks for the heads up and the logs. We're on it. Immediate plan:

1) Triage with infra (David) to confirm whether this is routing/NAT exhaustion or a firewall rule regression.
2) If NAT translation pool is saturated, we can temporarily scale Dedicated egress or add a secondary NAT route to reduce translation contention.
3) We'll open a support ticket and keep you updated every 30 minutes.

David/rishi: please jump in with initial findings and run a VPC peering connectivity and NAT allocation check; include any quick mitigation steps we can push without a config freeze on FinApps.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 08:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: 5xx/429 surge impacting checkout (FinApps)

Marissa — initial telemetry:
- Observed a retry amplification pattern from FinApps' IP range; upstream connections to our workers show repeated SYN retransmits followed by connection resets.
- NAT port pool for the customer's dedicated egress is at ~98% saturation in the last 30m.
- We also see intermittent DNS timeouts to internal name resolution for the worker fleet (flaky responses from the internal resolver).

Immediate mitigations I'm pushing now:
- Provisional increase to NAT port allocation for the FinApps dedicated pool (should reduce 429s from client-side retries).
- Rolling restart of the internal DNS resolver set in the region (low-risk, ~45s window).

I'm attaching the vpc-trace and a short slice of tcpdump. Will confirm once NAT capacity change is live.

-David
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: vpc-trace-20270509.txt (text/plain)
From: Rita Gomez <rita.gomez@finapps.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: 5xx/429 surge impacting checkout (FinApps)

Appreciate the quick action. A couple of asks from our side: 
- Can you provide a short note we can share with our CTO (timeline + what you're changing)?
- If you hit the NAT port limit again, can you fail traffic to our secondary region (us-west-2) while you remediate?

We're standing by and can throttle some client-side retries if you want us to do that as a temporary measure.

-Rita
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 10:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Executive escalation: FinApps 5xx/429 incident — ask for leadership alignment

Team — Rita has looped in her CTO and revenue ops. Given the revenue impact and the risk of further retry storms, I'd like to request quick alignment with Sales leadership and an exec liaison. Laura, can you join as the commercial exec onboarded for FinApps? Rishi, can you confirm whether we should offer temporary credits / SLA exceptions if the incident continues beyond 4 hours?

Notes for leadership:
- Likely root causes: NAT port exhaustion + transient DNS resolver instability triggering request timeouts and retry amplification.
- Short-term mitigations underway: NAT capacity bump and DNS resolver restart.
- Medium-term: consider persistent NAT sizing recommendations and optional Dedicated egress HA config for FinApps.

I will send a short one-pager to FinApps and their CTO once we have confirmation of mitigation.
—Marissa
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Rita Gomez <rita.gomez@finapps.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FinApps: Persistent 5xx/429 + VPC/NAT timeouts — executive engagement requested

Rita — thanks for flagging and for your patience. Executive update for your CTO: 

Summary: Over the morning we observed an elevated rate of 5xx/429 responses on your Dedicated endpoint. Redwood SRE identified NAT translation pool saturation combined with intermittent DNS resolution failures in the serving region. Immediate fixes were applied (NAT pool increase; DNS resolver restart) which substantially reduced 429s and latency. We are continuing to monitor.

Next steps and offers:
- Short-term: we recommend client-side retry throttling (1s backoff) if your retry logic is aggressive; we can share a quick config snippet.
- Medium-term: we will propose an egress HA configuration and persistent NAT sizing for your Dedicated pool; we'll follow up with an implementation timeline in a separate doc.
- Commercial: if the incident leads to measurable revenue loss, please open a billing case and we'll escalate to review credits.

We've attached a short timeline and the two artifacts David shared. Will remain in close contact.

Best,
Laura Bennett
VP, Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: finapps_incident_timeline.pdf (summary)
